en.title: Shortest Execution Time with a Gap Between Identical Tasks
en.description:
Each character is a task that takes 1 unit of time, and identical characters belong to the same type. You may reorder the tasks freely and insert idle time; two tasks of the same type must be separated by at least minGap full time units. Find the minimum time to finish all tasks.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains the lowercase task string; the second line contains minGap. The original snapshot gave no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤string length≤100000, 0≤minGap≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: Example 1: ab_ ab_ ab (spaces are only for grouping) takes 8 units, with 2 units between tasks of the same type. Example 2: there is no gap requirement, so the 6 tasks run back to back and the answer is 6. Example 3: a has 6 tasks, which need at least 16 units from the first to the last; other tasks can fill the gaps, so the answer is 16.
hints: Let f be the highest frequency and c the number of types that reach it; the answer is max(total tasks,(f−1)(minGap+1)+c).
